project.objective: Who was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont?

questions.question: What does William A. Bagley's death record of 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont say about his parentage?
questions.rationale: William's 1884 death record is the most direct primary source likely to name his parents. Vermont maintained vital records from 1857 onward; FamilySearch indexes and original town-clerk volumes cover this period. Answering this question first establishes whether a direct, contemporaneous statement of parentage exists before pursuing indirect evidence through census and probate records.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: q_001 is scoped to the content of the 1884 Vermont death record for William A. Bagley. That record (ark:/61903/1:1:XF8X-MVK, Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954, collection 1784223) was located via an indexed search (log_001), extracted into 15 assertions, and its parentage statements fully captured: Father = David Bagley; Mother = Sarah A. All assertions carry GPS three-layer classifications. Person-evidence links were created for all three personas (MJDL-Q8B, I1/David Bagley, LVDV-6MK). The remaining plan items (pli_002–pli_010) address broader corroboration beyond q_001's specific scope and were appropriately skipped. The question as stated is fully answered by this single-source search.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes — the 1884 Vermont death record explicitly names David Bagley as father and Sarah A. as mother of William A. Bagley. The question asked what the death record says; the record has been found and its content fully extracted.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch collection 1784223 (Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954) is the primary digitized repository for Vermont vital records of this period and jurisdiction. The target record was found at rank 1, matchScore 0.895, attachedToSubject:true. For a question scoped to one specific record, this repository search is sufficient.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: The indexed/simplified GedcomX entry was used via record_read; the original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYK4-VTM) was not consulted. This is a noted limitation: the index is a derivative, and the original image could in principle reveal additional detail or catch index transcription errors. The index typo 'Willaim' for 'William' is the only known transcription artifact; no parentage-field errors were identified.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Only one record was searched, which is definitionally sufficient for q_001 as stated (a question about a single record's content). A broader parentage proof question would require at least two independent sources; that is beyond q_001's scope.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 is an original civil register series (post-1857 statewide registration era). The death entry provides primary information for death facts and secondary/direct information for parentage (informant unidentified, reporting post-mortem). The parentage assertion meets the 'direct evidence of what the record states' standard for q_001.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No conflicts identified within this record. The record unambiguously names one father (David Bagley) and one mother (Sarah A.) with no competing assertions from the same source.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Near-zero for q_001 as scoped — no unsearched source could change what the 1884 death record itself states. Risk is moderate if the question is reframed as a parentage proof (secondary information, single source, original image not read, mother's maiden name only partially recorded as 'A.'). A follow-up question corroborating David Bagley's paternity via census, church, or probate records is recommended.

A birth or baptism record for William A. Bagley (~born 1815) would directly name his parents. Search Vermont Births and Christenings 1765-1908 (collection 1675544, index only). If William's father died in Topsham, his probate estate would name heirs including William. Topsham falls in the Bradford Probate District. Search Vermont Probate Files 1800-1921 (collection 1435692, indexed+images) for 'Bagley' in Orange County first, as it is indexed and searchable. A will or administration record naming William as a son/heir would be direct evidence of parentage.

A fulltext_search for 'Bagley' across these volumes could surface grantor/grantee entries naming William or his father. Land conveyances where the father deeded land to William would be direct evidence of the father-son relationship. Also Vermont Land Records, Early to 1900 (collection 1409123, images only).

Hamilton Child's Gazetteer of Orange County, Vt., 1762-1888 (FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog 3417524) contains biographical sketches of prominent Orange County residents and town histories. A Bagley entry could name family members including parents. This is a compiled derivative source but may provide leads and corroborating information not found in vital or census records. proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## What William A. Bagley’s 1884 Vermont Death Record States About His Parentage

**Conclusion (probable):** The 1884 Vermont death register entry for William A. Bagley names **David Bagley** as his father and **Sarah A.** (maiden surname not recorded) as his mother. This finding is graded *probable* — not proved — because the parentage information rests on secondary information from a single source with an unidentified informant, and the original register image was not separately examined.

### The Source

“Vermont, Vital Records, 1760-1954,” FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XF8X-MVK : accessed 31 July 2026), Entry for Willaim A. Bagley and David Bagley, 1884; image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYK4-VTM).

Vermont’s statewide civil vital registration began in 1857. This 1884 death entry falls within the registration period and is drawn from FamilySearch collection 1784223. The indexed entry was recovered at rank 1 (matchScore 0.895) and was already attached to William A. Bagley’s FamilySearch profile, confirming identity independently of the matching algorithm. The index title contains a transcription error (“Willaim” for “William”) that does not affect the parentage data.

### GPS Three-Layer Analysis

**Source classification — original.** The Vermont vital registers are original civil records created at the time of registration under statewide mandate. The FamilySearch entry is drawn from this original register series. The underlying register image at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYK4-VTM is available but was not separately consulted; the indexed data was used.

**Information quality — mixed.** Death date and place (31 May 1884, Vermont) carry **primary information** quality: recorded at or near the time of the event by the town registrar under official duty. Parentage data — father’s name David Bagley; mother’s name Sarah A. — carries **secondary information** quality: these biographical facts about events occurring approximately sixty-nine years before the death were reported post-mortem by an unidentified informant whose proximity to the birth event cannot be assessed. Secondary information is inherently less reliable than primary for facts the informant could not personally have witnessed.

**Evidence type — direct.** The record explicitly names “David Bagley” as father and “Sarah A.” as mother. No inference is required to extract the stated parentage claim; this is direct evidence of what the record asserts.

### Limitations

1. **Single source.** The parentage conclusion rests on one record. GPS Component 1 (reasonably exhaustive research) for a parentage *proof* requires corroboration from independent sources — census household listings showing William in David Bagley’s household, a baptism record, or the parents’ marriage record confirming the David Bagley / Sarah Andrews union. Those searches exceed the specific scope of q_001 and are recommended as the next research step.

2. **Secondary information for parentage.** Because the informant is unidentified and was reporting post-mortem about events that occurred decades earlier, the parentage data carries the inherent reliability limitations of secondary information. The father’s name, surname spelling, or identity could be misremembered or incorrectly recorded.

3. **Mother’s maiden name not recorded.** The record lists the mother only as “Sarah A.” — no maiden surname appears. An existing tree link (R4) already identifies Sarah Sally Andrews (LVDV-6MK, born 1777 Gloucester, Massachusetts; died 19 March 1847 Topsham, Vermont) as a parent of William A. Bagley (MJDL-Q8B). The “A.” in the death record is consistent with “Andrews” as a maiden-name initial, and the birth year of 1777 makes biological parenthood of a child born about 1815 plausible. However, this equivalence is inferential and is not confirmed by the death record alone. The mother’s full maiden name remains unresolved pending independent corroborating evidence.

4. **Original image not consulted.** The indexed/simplified GedcomX entry was used; the original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-DYK4-VTM) was not separately examined. Index transcription errors beyond the known “Willaim/William” typo are possible. Consulting the original image is recommended to verify the parentage field spellings.

### Tree Encoding

At the *probable* tier, the concluded parent-child relationship is encoded in the research tree:
- **R7**: ParentChild (I1 / David Bagley → MJDL-Q8B / William A. Bagley), sourced to S1 (Vermont, Vital Records, 1760–1954)
- **R8**: Couple (I1 / David Bagley ↔ LVDV-6MK / Sarah Sally Andrews), sourced to S1 at quality 2 (inferred from co-parentage; the couple’s marriage record has not been located)

### Conclusion

Based on a single original vital register entry that provides secondary/direct evidence of parentage, it is **probable** that William A. Bagley’s 1884 Vermont death record names **David Bagley** as his father. The mother is named as **Sarah A.**, provisionally identified with *probable* confidence as Sarah Sally Andrews (LVDV-6MK) already in the research tree. This conclusion answers q_001 as stated. It does not constitute a GPS-proved parentage determination; corroboration from at least one independent source providing primary information — such as a census record showing William in David Bagley’s household, or a church baptism record naming David Bagley as father — is required to advance the conclusion to *proved*.

Topsham falls in the Bradford Probate District (not Randolph). Search Bradford District Estate Files 1780-1915 (collection 1807377, 75,694 images, browse-only — no name index). FamilySearch has multiple Topsham vital records volumes indexed at 100%: IGN 007728020 (births/marriages/deaths 1857-1869, 44 images), IGN 005464890 (vital statistic indexes 1857-1896, 200 images), and IGN 005487650 (index of births 1857-1897, marriage indexes 1857-1894, death indexes 1857-1897, 2,180 images). Use record_search or fulltext_search on these.

Several large Topsham vital statistic index volumes (IGNs 007747453-007747456, 334-2,747 images each, covering 1775-1998) are 0% name-indexed but full-text searchable — use fulltext_search rather than record_search for these.

The 1820 and 1830 federal censuses listed heads of household only. To find William A. Bagley (~b. 1815) as a child in his father's household, search for male household heads in Topsham with a boy in the correct age bracket.

# Locality Guide: Topsham, Orange County, Vermont (1815–1884)

## Jurisdictional Context

Topsham is a town in Orange County, Vermont. Orange County was organized 18 October 1785 from Cumberland County. Prior to Vermont statehood (4 March 1791), Topsham was part of the Republic of Vermont. No boundary changes affect Topsham itself during the 1815–1884 research window.

**Probate jurisdiction:** Topsham falls in the **Bradford Probate District** (Bradford, Corinth, Fairlee, Newbury, Strafford, Thetford, Topsham, Vershire, West Fairlee). In 1994, the Bradford and Randolph Districts merged into the Orange District.

## Vital Records

- **Statewide registration** began 1857; town clerks had kept records since ~1760 but compliance and completeness varied.
- **FamilySearch indexed collections** (index + images): Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 (coll. 1784223); Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records 1732-2005 (coll. 1987653); Vermont Town Records 1850-2005 (coll. 1627819).
- **Topsham-specific indexed volumes on FamilySearch**: IGN 007728020 (births/marriages/deaths 1857-1869, 44 images, 100% indexed); IGN 005464890 (vital statistic indexes 1857-1896, 200 images, 100% indexed); IGN 005487650 (birth/marriage/death indexes 1857-1897, 2,180 images, 100% indexed).
- **Pre-1857 Topsham town records**: IGN 005464260 (town records 1771-1860, 265 images, 0% name-indexed, full-text searchable).
- **Key caveat on death records for finding parents**: Vermont death records before 1919 rarely name parents. William A. Bagley's 1884 death record very likely will NOT name his father — use it to confirm death date/place but do not rely on it for parentage.

## Census Records

- Federal census years applicable: 1820, 1830 (head of household only — look for a Bagley household with a boy aged 0-10 in 1820, or 10-15 in 1830); 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 (all household members listed from 1850).
- US federal censuses are fully indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- Vermont state censuses are limited; American Ancestors has some substitutes (1778-1822, 1840).

## Probate Records

- **Bradford District Estate Files 1780-1915** (coll. 1807377, 75,694 images, **browse-only — no name index**). This is the primary probate repository for Topsham. Must be browsed image-by-image.
- **Vermont Probate Files 1800-1921** (coll. 1435692, 10,225 records, indexed + images) — broader statewide index; check for Bagley entries.
- **Ancestry**: Vermont Wills and Probate Records 1749-1999 (paid subscription).

## Land Records

- **Vermont Land Records, Early to 1900** (coll. 1409123, images only, no index).
- **Topsham deed volumes on FamilySearch** (all full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed): IGN 007812519 (1841-1946/1849-1853), IGN 007812520 (1853-1859), IGN 007814131 (1859-1869), IGN 007814130 (1866-1878), IGN 004151751 (1882-1893), IGN 007814129 (1878-1883).
- Land records can identify the father's name if William bought or inherited land from him, or if father's estate sold land.

## Church Records

- FamilySearch Wiki notes church records as a key substitute when vital records are sparse. Topsham churches (Congregational, Methodist) may hold baptism/membership records; check FamilySearch catalog and Vermont Historical Society.

## Military Records

- Vermont Enrolled Militia Records 1861-1867 (coll. 1483040, indexed). William (~b. 1815) would be ~46-52 years old during the Civil War — too old for active service but may appear in enrollment.
- Revolutionary War pensioner census 1840 and War of 1812 pension records may be relevant if the father served.

## Newspapers and Obituaries

- Vermont newspapers 1800s-current on GenealogyBank and Newspapers.com (Ancestry, paid). An 1884 obituary for William A. Bagley may name his parents or surviving relatives.
- Chronicling America (Library of Congress) has some Vermont newspapers free.

## Gazetteers and Compiled Genealogies

- *Gazetteer of Orange County, Vt., 1762-1888* by Hamilton Child (FamilySearch Digital Library, catalog 3417524) — may contain biographical sketches naming parents.
- Vermont GenWeb (vtgenweb.org) and Genealogical Society of Vermont (genealogyvermont.org) for compiled resources.

## Key Access Notes

- Most Topsham vital index volumes are **full-text searchable** on FamilySearch even when not name-indexed — use `fulltext_search` with the image group number.
- Bradford District probate files are **browse-only** — plan to page through volumes if a Bagley probate entry is suspected.
- Ancestry and American Ancestors hold complementary collections requiring subscriptions (available free at FamilySearch centers).
